pr.title: Run CI reviews on your own runners, with the credential the runner holds
pr.head: 54c88dae7fe57b83c4e2ee54b8533a240364605d

summary: Projector can review each pull request in a GitHub Actions job. project init --ci-review writes the workflow, .github/workflows/projector-review.yml, and the composite action in actions/review/ runs an agent (Claude Code or Codex) that publishes the review. Until now that job always ran on a GitHub-hosted ubuntu-latest machine, with the agent's credential passed in from a repository secret.

This pull request lets the jobs run on self-hosted runners, machines the repository's owner controls. Such a runner can reach internal tools, such as a self-hosted Grafana, and can hold the agent's credential itself. Three things stood in the way, and the change removes each one:

1. The runner was hard-coded. A new setting, review.ci_runs_on, records runner labels, and init writes them into both jobs.
  2. Unset secrets hid the runner's own credential. A secret that is not set reads as an empty string, so CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }} blanked out a value the runner held. A new credential kind, runner, makes the workflow pass no secrets at all.
  3. Codex got a throwaway home on every job. A Codex ChatGPT login refreshes itself in auth.json, so a copy goes stale. The action now uses the runner's own Codex home in place when that is the credential.

A new page, docs/self-hosted-runners.md, explains setup and safety limits, and the review-in-ci plan records the decisions in a new § 10. The action's config input still appends to ~/.projector.toml on every job, which a persistent runner cannot tolerate; the docs work around it and the plan leaves a fix for later.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Hosted runner: a fresh GitHub machine per job, here ubuntu-latest.
  • Self-hosted runner: your own machine registered with GitHub; a job picks it by its labels.
  • Credential kind: subscription, api-key, or the new runner, recorded as review.ci_credential.
  • Codex home: $CODEX_HOME, or ~/.codex, where Codex keeps auth.json, config.toml, and skills.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html: The first Projector review, at 066bf19, requested changes with one finding: naming ubuntu-latest explicitly bypassed the guard that refuses a runner credential on a hosted runner. 54c88da fixed it with ci.hosted, and the review of that head is clean, with one suggestion: the init note about running review.gate on your runner should also check ci.hosted. The CI check job and review.gate passed on both heads.

groups.title: Generating the workflow
groups.kicker: Runner labels and the runner credential kind, from flags and settings into the workflow text
intro: ci.workflow_text renders the workflow from a template. It now takes two more inputs: the runner labels, which fill runs-on in both jobs, and the credential kind. When the kind is runner, the review step gets no env: block, so the agent sees the runner's own environment.

init and project review ci-workflow read the labels from --ci-runs-on/--runs-on, then review.ci_runs_on, and the kind from --ci-credential/--credential, then review.ci_credential. init records both, so a later plain init keeps the workflow the same.

checks.text: The workflow's second line is a digest of its text. init replaces a workflow whose digest still matches and keeps one somebody edited. Labels being part of the generated text is what lets a self-hosted workflow stay maintained by init.

files.note: Adds parse_runs_on/format_runs_on, the runner kind, hosted, which tells a GitHub-hosted runner's labels apart, and the guard in body that refuses runner on a hosted runner.

checks.text: hosted counts as hosted no labels at all, or only labels of GitHub's images (ubuntu-*, macos-*, windows-*) without self-hosted. It does not require self-hosted, because a runner registered with --no-default-labels and an Actions Runner Controller scale set do not carry it.

The guard now uses hosted(runs_on), so --ci-runs-on ubuntu-latest with a recorded runner credential is refused rather than writing a hosted workflow with no secrets. The review at 54c88da traced it, and the new subtests cover it.

files.note: New flags on init and review ci-workflow, the ci_runs_on and ci_credential resolvers, recording both settings, and set_ci_secrets setting no credential secret for runner while still handling an app's private key.
Both runs-on lines become @RUNS_ON@, and the env: header moves into @ENV@ so it can be left out.

checks.text: With no labels and no runner kind, the rendered workflow is the same as before apart from the header comment: the old template joined env lines and added a blank line, and the new one ends each env line with a newline, giving the same bytes. Checked by comparing the two templates' substitution.

groups.title: The review action on a runner
groups.kicker: The credential check and install step learn about a runner's own login and CLI
intro: The action's first step checks that the agent has exactly one credential. For Codex it now also counts an auth.json in the runner's Codex home, when no CODEX_AUTH_JSON secret is set, and refuses that login beside OPENAI_API_KEY. With no credential, the error names what to set up on a self-hosted runner.

The install step skips npm install --global when the CLI on PATH already prints the pinned version as a whole word. When the runner's Codex login is the credential, the step exports that home as CODEX_HOME, links Projector's skills in as skills/projector, and never writes auth.json. Every hosted path is unchanged.

files.note: Credential check and install step changes for a runner-held Codex login and a preinstalled CLI.

checks.text: This branch runs only when neither Codex secret is set, which the credential check above allows only when auth.json exists in the same home. Linking into skills/projector rather than replacing skills keeps Codex's own skills/.system in place.

groups.title: Documentation and the plan
groups.kicker: A new guide for self-hosted runners, the reference updates, and plan § 10
intro: docs/self-hosted-runners.md walks through deciding whether you need a runner, preparing it, pointing the workflow at it, giving it each agent's credential, preinstalling the CLI, reaching internal tools, and safety limits: private repositories only, ephemeral runners where possible, a restricted runner group, and read-only tokens. It names the prompt-injection risk that sets those limits.

docs/cli.md and docs/review-in-ci.md document the new flags and settings and link to the guide. The review-in-ci plan, still in-progress, gains § 9 bullets and a new § 10 without renumbering earlier sections.

files.note: New guide to running reviews on self-hosted runners.
Adds the runner credential kind and a short section that links to the guide.
Documents --ci-runs-on, --ci-credential runner, --runs-on, --credential, and the two settings.
Plan § 9 bullets for what implementation settled, and new § 10 on self-hosted runners.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: Init, workflow, and action-step tests for the new paths
intro: The new tests drive init in temporary repositories and run the action's bash steps with fake claude, codex, and npm binaries on PATH. They cover labels surviving a refresh, a runner credential passing no secret, the refusal on a hosted runner (no labels, or only GitHub image labels such as ubuntu-latest), moving a runner credential back to a hosted runner, runners GitHub does not host (a scale set name, custom labels, and Self-Hosted), the Codex login counting as a credential, the exact-version install skip, and the runner's Codex home being reused across two jobs.
